subject: Post-demo: model fit triage, regression signals, and pinning plan

Cc: procurement@deltaretail.com
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model fit questions & recent output drift

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for walking us through the demo this morning. The personalization examples looked promising and the latency numbers were great. After running a quick A/B on a small slice of live traffic (search personalization, curated recommenders) we noticed an uptick in hallucination-like outputs and format regressions starting ~48 hours after your last patch.

Before we invest further in integration, can you:
- Share the evaluation artifacts and prompt set you used in the demo?
- Recommend model variants you think match our recall/precision tradeoff for short-form product descriptions (we care more about factual precision than creativity)
- Confirm whether there was a model or runtime version change this week and whether we can pin or rollback quickly if needed

We have a short internal review tomorrow morning and would appreciate an immediate triage plan. If this is expected behavior from a quantization tweak, we need to know the expected delta on edge cases.

Attached: sample outputs (redacted) and a short failure log.

Thanks —
Claire Henderson
Head of Search & Personalization
DeltaRetail

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit questions & recent output drift

Claire — thanks for the clear notes and for running that A/B. I'm sorry to hear you saw regression signals after the patch. Immediate answers and next steps below.

Quick answers:
- Eval artifacts & prompts: attaching the prompt suite (deltaretail_prompt_suite_v3.jsonl) and the standalone eval report (deltaretail_eval_report_20260330.pdf). Also shared a Drive folder with all logs (link below).
- Recommended variants: for DeltaRetail's precision-first use case we recommend trying redwood-alpha-13b-v1.8 (unquantized) and redwood-alpha-13b-q4-v2 (4-bit quantized but with calibration). If token cost is a concern, redwood-alpha-7b-v1.2-cal is another option but expect slightly lower factual recall.
- Was there a change?: We rolled a minor runtime kernel update to the hosted fleet yesterday evening that was meant to improve batching latency. That update touched kernel selection for key/value cache handling and some quantization code paths on 13B-class models. We are investigating whether the change reduces fidelity on certain short-answer formats.

Short-term triage (today):
1) Pin your production route to redwood-alpha-13b-v1.8 (previous stable) — this is reversible in <30m.
2) Run the attached regression harness (we included the test prompts) against both v1.8 and the current v1.9 runtime patch and upload diffs to the shared Drive.
3) We will run a focused golden-prompt canary in a dedicated capacity to measure latency/cost changes and edge-case regressions.

Longer-term: if the kernel change is the root cause we will either back out the kernel in the fleet or release a calibrated quantization patch. We will also provide you a pinning playbook (attached) that includes API calls and console steps.

Proposed immediate timeline: pin now, run regression harness (2h), follow-up call with triage results by 6pm PT. Is 5:30pm PT OK for a quick sync?

Monica Patel
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
m: +1-415-555-0199

Attachments: deltaretail_prompt_suite_v3.jsonl, deltaretail_eval_report_20260330.pdf, pinning_playbook.md

Looping in the ops runbook pieces and quick commands — Claire, you should be able to switch the model version from the Console under Routes > Production > DeltaRetail-search or via API: 

Console: Production route -> Edit -> "Model version" -> select redwood-alpha-13b-v1.8 -> Save (change takes effect in ~5-10m)
API snippet (curl):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/{route_id}/pin \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-13b-v1.8"}'

Rollback note: If you want an emergency rollback we can pin to the previous stable within 30 minutes and route 100% to it. I will kick off the regression harness on a copy of your prompt set immediately and upload CSV diffs to the Drive folder. Expected run time ~90–120 minutes for the full suite.

Caveats: the quantized v2 path improves token throughput but in our internal fuzz tests it can change punctuation/abbreviation handling for short product codes — that sounds consistent with the samples you shared. If we pin to v1.8 we should also run parity checks on tokenization-sensitive prompts.

Ben Carter
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
